thesis_pillars.text: Chips are the building blocks for the digital economy. They are pervasive, powering everything from smartphones and computers to datacenters, cars and medical devices. Global semiconductor sales have grown mid-single-digits annually for decades to $800bn in 2025, expected to top $1tn this year. Wafer fabrication equipment sales (including lithography machines) have grown high-single-digits annually since the late 1980s, with acceleration in recent years (5-year CAGR is 15.8%). WFE is high-teens as a percent of global semi sales (and growing), and lithography represents 25-30% of total WFE spend (and growing).

thesis_pillars.pillar: Monopoly in EUV lithography with an impregnable moat
terms: Monopoly in EUV lithography with an impregnable moat
thesis_pillars.text: ASML dominates its part of the value chain, with 90% of the DUV lithography market and 100% of EUV. The other two competitors in DUV are Nikon and Canon. ASML benefits from a system of interlocking barriers that make its position nearly impossible to replicate. Their technology is the embodiment of accumulated engineering knowledge across hundreds of interdependent subsystems (laser physics, vacuum engineering, mirror optics, etc.) which took decades of effort and significant resources to master. Switching costs are high (in time in and in money) as they co-develop technology roadmaps with customers who have each invested billions into integration. The services component deepens their already entrenched customer relationships.

management.value: Management and capital allocation: President and CEO Christophe Fouquet joined ASML in 2008 and held several management positions in marketing and product management prior to CEO, including Chief Business Officer from 2022 to 2024, EVP of EUV from 2018 to 2022 and EVP of Applications from 2013 to 2018. Prior to ASML, he worked at industry peers KLA Tencor and Applied Materials. Executives are long-tenured with decades of accumulated technical knowledge. While CFO Roger Dassen comes from a pure finance and audit background (previously at Deloitte), there are mostly engineers at the top (the CEO has a physics background, and the CTO is a mathematician). On capital allocation, the hierarchy follows a fairly classic framework for a capital-light, high-margin industrial business. Priorities include 1) reinvesting back into the business, with R&D treated as sacrosanct and cap ex spend to scale production capacity, and 2) returning excess capital to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks. Over the last three decades, they’ve spent nearly €34bn on a cumulative basis on R&D, which is consistently low- to mid-teens as a percent of total sales. This spend is not discretionary, but rather the engine that sustains the monopoly. Since the mid-1990s, ASML has spent nearly €15bn on cap ex on a cumulative basis (typically mid- to high-single-digits as a percent of sales) to ensure sufficient manufacturing capacity to build enough machines to meet demand. ASML has returned €16.7bn in dividends over the last two decades, and they’ve repurchased €28.2bn in stock over that same time frame. Nearly 75% of buybacks have occurred in the last five years. While M&A is not a priority, ASML has made selective, strategic acquisitions over time, mostly to internalize critical technology dependencies (for example, acquiring Cymer for their industry leading laser light sources).

sentences.text: In April 2025 ASML demonstrated the first ever 1,000-watt light source for EUV lithography, built on 25 years of engineering advancements.
In March 2025 ASML signed a five-year strategic partnership agreement with imec focused on sustainable innovation in Europe.
ASML is expanding its global footprint by broadening supplier bases in Asia and enhancing manufacturing in Europe, Asia and the US.
Securing a successful ERP migration is a stated priority to enable scaling and drive improvements in cost, quality and compliance.
ASML plans to initiate sales and support operations in countries where it does not currently have them, such as India.
Counterparty credit risk is concentrated: the three largest customers accounted for €1,294.2 million or 35.4% of accounts receivable and finance receivables at December 31, 2025.
Carl Zeiss SMT is the sole supplier of optics, and if it terminated supply or could not maintain production, ASML "would effectively cease to be able to conduct our business".
US trade measures restrict supply of specific products and services, and the list of restricted entities remains subject to change and may be further expanded.
For 2026 ASML expects full-year revenue between €34 billion and €39 billion and gross margin between 51% and 53%.
Logic-related revenues are expected to remain strong and Memory revenues to be significantly higher compared to 2025.
EUV revenue is anticipated to be significantly higher, driven by advanced node ramps, while non-EUV revenue is expected to be similar to 2025.
First-quarter 2026 guidance is total net sales between €8.2 billion and €8.9 billion, gross margin between 51% and 53%, R&D costs of around €1.2 billion and SG&A costs of around €0.3 billion.
For 2030 ASML sees an opportunity to achieve annual revenue between approximately €44 billion and €60 billion with gross margin between approximately 56% and 60%.
Management expects global semi sales to grow at 9% CAGR (2025-2030) and surpass $1 trillion by 2030.
